title_options: Why Your Agent Reads Old Facts After a Memory Update
The Write Succeeded; the Next Read Returned the Old Fact
Agent Memory Writes Land Before the Index Sees Them
presentation.title_rationale: The reader problem is a memory update that was acknowledged and then contradicted by the next read. The selected title names the symptom (old facts after a memory update) in 52 characters and promises one supported benefit: understanding and locating that gap. It claims no fix, no percentage and no timing figure; the 11-configuration sweep and the measured window stay in the description and the introduction, which is where the earlier 96-character headline had crammed them.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover is a three-step conceptual chain taken from the article's own argument: a write is acknowledged by the record store, the store becomes visible only when the derived index commits, and the next read happens after that. Its caption tells the reader what to do (measure the gap) and it labels itself a conceptual checklist rather than measurement data, so it explains the mechanism without asserting any of the recorded milliseconds.
